# bugs #3843: mcs51: Branching Range Exceeded for jumps across inline assembler lines with a semicolon directly after the mnemonic

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3843/
- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Apply the first patch and close. Decide separately on the second patch, which is for another cause of the message.
- Patch: [bugs-3843-1.patch](../../patches/bugs-3843-1.patch). Applies to r17176 without the other patches.
- Patch: [bugs-3843-2.patch](../../patches/bugs-3843-2.patch). Applies to r17176 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The ticket's file is `firmware/src/usrp2/usrp_main.c` of libusrp 3.4.10. A compiler built from
r15242, which is SDCC 4.5.0, was given the ticket's options, and the assembler reports the ticket's
message at the ticket's line. Line 1389 of `usrp_main.asm` is `jz 00140$` in `main_loop`, and the
label is 131 bytes before it. A compiler built from r17158 compiles the file, but it has the
defect, and the first test under Verification fails with it. SDCC 4.2.0 was not tested.

## Cause

`asmLineNodeFromLineNode` in `src/mcs51/main.c` computes the size of each assembler line.
`pcDistance` in `src/SDCCpeeph.c` adds these sizes when a peephole rule asks whether a label is in
range of a short jump. After the mnemonic, `asmLineNodeFromLineNode` returns without a size when
the next character is `;`, `:`, or `=`. That is correct for a label, an assignment, and a comment
line. In `nop; nop; nop;` the comment begins directly after the mnemonic, so the line got size 0.
The assembler reads it as one `nop` of 1 byte.

The firmware's `SYNCDELAY` macro is `__asm nop; nop; nop; __endasm`, and four of these lines are
between the `jz` and its label. The peephole optimizer counted no bytes for them and replaced the
long jump by a short one. The condition is from r3236 (2004), so 4.2.0 has it too. A jump fails
only when the bytes that were not counted decide whether its label is in range.

The message has a second cause, which the ticket's file does not exercise. `labelJTInRange` in
`src/SDCCpeeph.c` decides whether the mcs51 rules 260.a to 260.m replace the `ljmp` instructions of
a jump table by `sjmp`. It compared the distance of each case label with one limit, and that limit
increases with the index of the table entry. That is right for a label after the table, which is
nearer to later entries. A label before the table is farther from later entries, so the function
accepted labels that are out of range of the `sjmp` in a later entry.

## Fix

The first patch fixes the ticket. `asmLineNodeFromLineNode` returns at a semicolon only when no
mnemonic precedes it.

The second patch concerns the jump table. For a label before the table, `labelJTInRange` computes
the distance from the label to the end of the entry's `sjmp` in the replacement and accepts at
most 127 bytes. The check for labels after the table is not changed.

## Decision

The second patch is separable. It changes another file, it has its own test, and the ticket's
file compiles without it.

Its limit for a label before the table is 127 bytes. The offset of `sjmp` allows 128 bytes
backward from the end of the instruction. The patch uses 127 because `labelInRange` and the other
branch of `labelJTInRange` use 127 for both directions. A table with a case label exactly 128
bytes before the end of an entry's jump therefore keeps its `ljmp` instructions, which are 1 byte
longer per entry. A limit of 128 would allow `sjmp` there. It was not tested.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-3843.c` has a backward and a forward jump across 140 lines of
`nop; nop; nop;`. Without the first patch, the assembler reports the message for both jumps. This
was run for mcs51 with the small, medium, large, and huge models and with `--stack-auto` in the
small and large models. With the patch, the test passes with these six sets of options and on
host, stm8, and z80, where it has no inline assembler. The first patch was also applied to r15242.
That compiler compiles the ticket's file, with `jnz 00243$` and `ljmp 00140$` in place of the `jz`.

`support/regression/tests/bug-3843-2.c` has a `switch` in a loop, with one case label at the top
of the loop and 110 `nop` instructions between that label and the jump table. With the first patch
alone, it does not assemble with any of the six sets of mcs51 options. With both patches it passes
with them and on host, stm8, and z80. At the limit, a table has `sjmp` instructions when its label
is 127 bytes back and `ljmp` instructions when the label is 128 or more bytes back.

## Related

- The entry local 0006 describes a third cause of this message on mcs51. With peephole rule
  257.c, the optimizer replaces `sjmp` by `ljmp`, which is 1 byte longer, without a range check.
  The two patches do not change that.
- `src/ds390/main.c` and `src/hc08/main.c` have the same condition in their line parsers. This
  was read from the source. Neither file is changed, and the two ports were not tested.
